transitionalWaiver.reason: v2026.1023.0 predates the managed Codex project-auth implementation. Porting the deployed patch stack to that tag would require a substantive rewrite with no operational benefit.
transitionalWaiver.replaceWith: The first stable tag that contains the managed Codex project-auth patch stack

patches.retireWhen: The stable base contains all six commits or patch-equivalent changes.
patches.notes: Scopes managed Codex project-auth checks to the task project and uses the Harness project-auth policy for routed accounts. The deploy commits were produced on canary.7; the upstream PR was rebased onto canary.8 on 2026-10-24. Both stacks have the same patch IDs. Adds the upstream follow-up that preserves invalid probe-directory diagnostics without starting the adapter. Ten new regression cases cover direct and routed Codex plus the HTTP route. The sixth upstream/deploy commits have matching patch IDs.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base contains the macOS remote process identity fix and signal ownership checks or patch-equivalent changes.
patches.notes: Adds Darwin boot/start process evidence and portable timestamps. Stop and failed-launch cleanup verify live ownership, including before KILL escalation. The upstream and deployment commits have matching patch IDs.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base distinguishes isolated Claude user settings from project authentication with equivalent local and shell-backed remote coverage.
patches.notes: Deployment-specific conservative boundary: reject project authentication from the physical task directory through ancestors below the host home. Managed CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR replaces the host user settings. Retain this small port while upstream Claude settings-source discovery evolves.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base contains the five portable test baseline commits or patch-equivalent changes.
patches.notes: Test-only portability fixes for native Git diagnostics, npm pack metadata, loaded fixture waits, uninstall host-home isolation, and macOS TCP admission. The deploy and upstream stacks have matching patch IDs. The full local baseline completed with 42662 tests passed, 158 existing conditional skips, and zero final failures after full-scope repairs. No new skip or waiver was added. Adds a stdin-gated native lifetime fixture after CI exposed a bootstrap signal-registration race. Controlled normal, early-exit, and assertion-failure paths left no snapshots or processes.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted upstream review workflow supports forks without an upstream private App key and reads review scripts from the trusted PR base commit.
patches.notes: Preserves Dependency Review, all quality gates, and the current permission set. Forks use the built-in workflow token; the upstream repository keeps its App token. Signed Actions comments are updated across retries.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base contains both commits from paperclipai/paperclip#17683 or patch-equivalent changes.
patches.notes: Makes the inbox failed-run list and the sidebar badge apply one resolved-interruption rule. The run list accepts suppressResolvedFailures, and issue status changes refresh the filtered run query. Deploy and upstream commits have matching patch IDs.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base compares managed bindings by normalized identity and resolves prospective environment variables before adoption checks, with equivalent permission and selection-change tests.
patches.notes: Local hotfix for the pinned canary adoption and legacy-adapter interfaces. Port the behavior separately for upstream review rather than publish this installation-specific diff as an upstream backport. Ordinary environment edits do not start a provider probe; actual model, harness, binding, or execution-environment changes still validate. Both probe paths use the same secret resolver after execution-target validation. Unavailable targets retain missing-binding diagnostics through metadata-only inspection without resolving secret values. Upstream contribution: https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/17760 (issue #17759; related #14518). The upstream port adds selection regressions and follows current contribution rules; this entry retains the original deploy commits and does not claim patch-ID equivalence.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base isolates workspace fallback fixtures from host-installed CLI commands and shell startup PATH changes with equivalent assertions.
patches.notes: Test-only isolation: controlled PATH and /bin/sh prevent a globally installed CLI from consuming synthetic fallback config. Real dependency installs still use pnpm and retain their exit status. No production fallback or fail-closed behavior changes. Preserve the original pnpm launcher location so relative Linux launchers resolve their own package; quote the absolute path without relocating it.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base isolates the company import/export fixture from package-registry update checks and records bounded startup failure timing with equivalent assertions.
patches.notes: Test-only configuration and diagnostics. Restore PAPERCLIP_UPDATE_CHECK=0 after clearing inherited Paperclip variables, capture relative output times and the last health result. Retain the original 30-second health deadline, 60-second setup bound, and import/export assertions. The CI timeout preceded listener readiness; the update query is a confirmed external dependency, not a proven sole cause.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted upstream stable base supplies an equivalent company-level reference-rate editor and a separate estimate report for gateway and subscription usage.
patches.notes: Withdrawn at the operator request on 2026-10-26. The second commit reverses the reference-rate API, shared estimator, Providers editor, and related feature documentation from PR #17. Preserve the executed SQL migration, journal, snapshots, and schema as inert compatibility history. The running service and database were restored to the pre-r7 r6 baseline. A full billing proposal remains local until upstream scope review; no new billing feature is approved or implemented.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base carries an equivalent bounded structured launch-policy contract, frozen recovery identity and old-artifact rejection on both controller and Runner.
patches.notes: Carry the reviewed transport repair against the pinned canary.7 deployment pair. Preserves all assigned skill roots and argv bounds; fixed CLI and real old-artifact qualifications pass. Upstream integration must preserve the complete recovery and permission contract rather than cherry-picking only argv removal. Static contract imports preserve the server scenario closure. Canonical Copilot v59 identity records changed shared launch sources; all prior identity fixtures remain unchanged. v59 is pending live Copilot qualification and is not part of the Codex/Claude/OpenCode pilot. Synthetic handoff and damaged-session recovery fixtures implement the real preflight and assert its order before thread admission.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base provides equivalent closed managed-Claude build/review policies, selected-skill discovery and fail-closed tool/sandbox boundaries.
patches.notes: Adapter-owned settings are needed for the managed connection authentication boundary on the pinned deployment. Raw settings remain rejected. Source regressions and real macOS CLI tool/file/network qualification pass; live saved-agent lifecycle remains a rollout gate. The workspace-build profile derives seven private workspace cache variables, including XDG_RUNTIME_DIR for pnpm per-user operation locks; it adds no write grant. Exact-root cleanup requires the current provider stop and successful collection. Candidate-review remains read-only. Fixed CLI synthetic offline install and boundary qualification passed; provider quality and live task lifecycle remain separate.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base gives managed SSH Codex runs equivalent private writable environment/cache projection and evidence-gated exact-run cleanup.
patches.notes: Carry target-host environment isolation for the current managed remote adapter. Preserves executable PATH, authentication home and configured model/effort. Targeted cleanup/restore regressions pass; actual remote toolchain and platform finalization are separate acceptance gates. Both supported pnpm 12 store aliases point to the same owned run directory. Three-host synthetic offline tar installation verified actual private CAS writes, artifact loading and exact cleanup; this is not a model task or product dependency qualification.

patches.retireWhen: The accepted stable base normalizes confirmed remote optional-file absence without swallowing permission, transport, timeout or local SSH setup errors.
patches.notes: The managed routed home can legitimately have no auth.json. One bounded metadata probe maps only proven absence to ENOENT, preserving successful provider output and host authentication. Synthetic POSIX/transport regressions pass; no credential contents or data migration.
